title: Gobind is everything
hook: sabh gobind hai: everything is Gobind; there is nothing without Him (Asa, Namdev, ang 485)

segments.voice: Yesterday Namdev sat at the back wall and sang, and the temple turned to face him. Your line was the temple turned. Who did you turn toward? Day seven hundred seventy-one.

Snap the cord of a necklace and you learn something fast. The beads go everywhere: under the couch, into the rug, one rolling off toward the door. While the cord held, you barely noticed it. You were looking at the beads. Namdev, the printer who sang his way into the Guru Granth Sahib, reached for exactly that picture. Yesterday the temple turned toward him. Today he turns the question around: where, in the whole world, is the Lord not? His answer, in the original, is short. Everything is Gobind.
screen: `A SNAPPED NECKLACE.` → `THE CORD YOU NEVER NOTICED.` → `WHERE IS THE LORD NOT?`

segments.voice: The hymn is in Raag Asa, on Ang 485, and its refrain is sabh gobind hai, sabh gobind hai, gobind bin nahi koi. In paraphrase: everything is Gobind, everything is Gobind; without Gobind there is nothing at all. Gobind is one of the names for the Lord in the Granth. Namdev gives two pictures for it. The first is the necklace. As one thread runs through countless beads, he says in paraphrase, so the Lord runs through everything, warp and weft. The second is water. Waves, foam and bubbles, he says, are not separate from the water. They rise and fall and look like many things, but they're water all the way through. Now the second turn. Namdev admits this isn't obvious. In the same hymn he says the world's dazzling pictures keep people bewildered, and only a rare one understands. That's honest. On plenty of days we see beads, not thread, waves, not water. And the third turn is what he does about it. He says the Guru's teaching woke his mind, and then he invites the listener: look at the Lord's creation, and think it over in your heart. In every heart, within all, there is only the One. Notice the word think. Namdev isn't asking us to pretend the beads aren't there. The colors, the people, the dishes in the sink, all stay. He's asking us to notice the thread through them. Sikhs sing this hymn as gurbani. Its whole teaching fits on one line. Everything is Gobind.
screen: `SABH GOBIND HAI.` · `ONE THREAD THROUGH ALL THE BEADS.` · `WAVES, FOAM, BUBBLES: ALL WATER.` · `ONLY A RARE ONE SEES IT.` · then, large: `EVERYTHING IS GOBIND.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: see Him in three things. Sit where you can look around. Let your eyes land on one thing nearby, anything, a cup, a window, your own hand. Rest on it for a few breaths, and say inside, sabh gobind hai. Then a second thing, farther away. Then a third, a sound, or a person, or the air itself. Don't force a feeling. Just let Namdev's line be the thread you run through the three. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Gobind is everything. Namdev's refrain, sabh gobind hai: the one thread through the beads, the water in every wave.
Your line: everything is gobind. Today, when something ordinary catches your eye, a crowd, a meal, a rainstorm, look once for the thread. Day seven hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Namdev's hymn with the refrain sabh gobind hai is sung in kirtan as gurbani, and Sikhs draw on it to speak of the One present in every heart and all of creation.

fork.setup: you're Namdev, trying to show how the One can be in so many different things. which picture do you reach for?
options: a king and his many soldiers.
one thread running through countless beads.
a mountain seen from far away.
fork.reveal: the thread through the beads, warp and weft, and then water in every wave, foam and bubble.

original.note: Gurmukhi: Gobind, a name for the Lord in Namdev's refrain sabh gobind hai.

trapdoor: what you thought: a poetic way of saying God is big.
what it means: Namdev sees the One running through everything, like a thread through beads and water through waves.
what a scholar hears: Asa, Ang 485: the refrain sabh gobind hai, and the line that only a rare one understands through the world's dazzle.

notes: Hymn 'ek anek biaapak poorak... sabh gobind hai sabh gobind hai gobind bin nahee koee; soot ek man sat sahans jaise ot pot prabh soee; jal tarang ar phen budbudaa jal te bhinn na hoee... kahat naamdeu har kee rachnaa dekhahu ridai beechaaree; ghat ghat antar sarab nirantar kebal ek muraaree' at Asa, Namdev, Ang 485: confirm Ang and paraphrases.
'Sat sahans' (hundreds/thousands of beads) rendered 'countless beads' to avoid a number.
'The Guru's teaching woke his mind' paraphrases 'gur updesee jaagat hee man maaniaa'; confirm reading of 'gur' here.
Removed a word count of the refrain under the claims rule.
Day 260 (y1) used Farid's 'Creator in creation'; this day uses Namdev's thread and water images instead.
